dedupe_keys.name: varginha brazil landfill biogas energy potential and greenhouse gas emissions of municipal solid waste scenarios

description: This case study evaluates energy recovery from landfill biogas and compares the greenhouse gas emissions and energy use of waste management options in Varginha, a city in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil. Alessandra Ribeiro de Souza and co-authors published it in 2019 in Engenharia Sanitária e Ambiental on the SciELO platform, with supporting tables deposited on SciELO's figshare. Waste generation and landfill operation were projected over 20 years, biogas production was estimated with the LandGEM software, economic feasibility was assessed with net present value and internal rate of return, and emissions were estimated with the US EPA Waste Reduction Model (WARM) for the current practice and three alternatives mixing recycling, anaerobic digestion, landfilling and incineration with energy recovery. The article is free to read on SciELO, and the supplementary data are free under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Coverage is one municipal landfill and its catchment. Caveats: results depend on LandGEM defaults and WARM factors developed for the United States. Only energy recovery at 150 kW was economically viable; scenario 3, with recovery of recyclables, anaerobic digestion and incineration, gave the largest environmental benefit, and recycling gave the largest energy gains and emission removals. Simulation uses: biogas yields, project economics and scenario emissions for landfill energy and waste strategy models. Related records: LandGEM (model-landgem) and the Lahore and Rawalpindi LandGEM study (case_study-lahore-rawalpindi-landfill-methane-leachate-landgem) use the same gas model.
